phases.name: Opener
phases.description: The first 15 to 60 seconds: who you are, why you are calling or meeting, and whether the buyer chooses to keep listening.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.description: Questions that uncover the buyer's situation, problems, priorities, budget and decision process before pitching.

phases.name: Objection handling
phases.description: How the rep responds to pushback, doubt, price challenges and brush-offs.

phases.name: Close
phases.description: Asking for a clear, specific next step, and handling the answer, including a no.

scoreAnchors.0-2: Missing or harmful: the move was absent when it was needed, or it actively damaged the call.
scoreAnchors.3-4: Weak: attempted but generic, rushed, or off-method.
scoreAnchors.5-6: Adequate: did the basic job, with clear room to improve.
scoreAnchors.7-8: Strong: specific, well-timed, and true to the method.
scoreAnchors.9-10: Excellent: would work on a demanding real buyer; hard to improve.

notReachedRule: If the call ended before a phase happened, mark it not reached and score it 0, and say why it was not reached (often that is the lesson).
ethicsRules: Flag any claim not supported by the product facts (invented numbers, customers or features).
Flag best-case results presented as typical.
Flag invented urgency, fake scarcity or fake deadlines.
Flag pretexts (pretending to know someone, claiming a meeting was agreed when it was not).
Flag pushing past a clear no.
Flag unauthorised discounts or promises the rep cannot keep.
ethicsPenalty: A deceptive move caps the score of the phase it occurred in at 4, however well it worked on the buyer.
